passages.text: Then Jacob called for his sons and said, “Gather around so that I can tell you what will happen to you in the days to come: Come together and listen, O sons of Jacob; listen to your father Israel.
passages.sermon:
Jacob was the father of twelve sons.
Jacob was also called Israel.
Jacob called his sons to come to him.
Jacob said, “Gather around me.”
Jacob said, “I will tell you what will happen to you in the future.”
Jacob said, “Come together and listen, sons of Jacob.”
Jacob said, “Listen to your father Israel.”
passages.original: וַיִּקְרָ֥א יַעֲקֹ֖ב אֶל־ בָּנָ֑יו וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הֵאָֽסְפוּ֙ וְאַגִּ֣ידָה לָכֶ֔ם אֵ֛ת אֲשֶׁר־ יִקְרָ֥א אֶתְכֶ֖ם בְּאַחֲרִ֥ית הַיָּמִֽים׃ הִקָּבְצ֥וּ וְשִׁמְע֖וּ בְּנֵ֣י יַעֲקֹ֑ב וְשִׁמְע֖וּ אֶל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֥ל אֲבִיכֶֽם׃

passages.text: Reuben, you are my firstborn, my might, and the beginning of my strength, excelling in honor, excelling in power.
passages.sermon:
Reuben, you are my firstborn son.
You are my strength.
You are the first of my children.
You have more honor than the others.
You have more power than the others.
passages.original: רְאוּבֵן֙ בְּכֹ֣רִי אַ֔תָּה כֹּחִ֖י וְרֵאשִׁ֣ית אוֹנִ֑י יֶ֥תֶר שְׂאֵ֖ת וְיֶ֥תֶר עָֽז׃

passages.text: Uncontrolled as the waters, you will no longer excel, because you went up to your father’s bed, onto my couch, and defiled it.
passages.sermon:
Reuben is Jacob’s firstborn son.
Reuben acted without control.
Reuben was unstable like water.
Reuben will not excel anymore.
Reuben went up to his father’s bed.
Reuben defiled his father’s couch.
passages.original: פַּ֤חַז כַּמַּ֙יִם֙ אַל־ תּוֹתַ֔ר כִּ֥י עָלִ֖יתָ מִשְׁכְּבֵ֣י אָבִ֑יךָ אָ֥ז חִלַּ֖לְתָּ יְצוּעִ֥י עָלָֽה׃פ

passages.text: Simeon and Levi are brothers; their swords are weapons of violence.
passages.sermon:
Simeon and Levi are brothers.
They use weapons.
Their weapons are violent.
Their swords bring harm.
passages.original: שִׁמְע֥וֹן וְלֵוִ֖י אַחִ֑ים כְּלֵ֥י חָמָ֖ס מְכֵרֹתֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: May I never enter their council; may I never join their assembly. For they kill men in their anger, and hamstring oxen on a whim.
passages.sermon:
Jacob speaks about Simeon and Levi.
Simeon and Levi are brothers.
They use violence.
Jacob does not want to join their council.
He does not want to be part of their assembly.
Simeon and Levi kill men when they are angry.
They cripple oxen when they choose.
passages.original: בְּסֹדָם֙ אַל־ תָּבֹ֣א נַפְשִׁ֔י בִּקְהָלָ֖ם אַל־ תֵּחַ֣ד כְּבֹדִ֑י כִּ֤י בְאַפָּם֙ הָ֣רְגוּ אִ֔ישׁ וּבִרְצֹנָ֖ם עִקְּרוּ־ שֽׁוֹר׃

passages.text: Cursed be their anger, for it is strong, and their wrath, for it is cruel! I will disperse them in Jacob and scatter them in Israel.
passages.sermon:
Simeon and Levi are brothers.
They have strong anger.
Their anger is cursed.
Their wrath is cruel.
Their wrath is cursed.
I will divide them in Jacob.
I will scatter them in Israel.
passages.original: אָר֤וּר אַפָּם֙ כִּ֣י עָ֔ז וְעֶבְרָתָ֖ם כִּ֣י קָשָׁ֑תָה אֲחַלְּקֵ֣ם בְּיַעֲקֹ֔ב וַאֲפִיצֵ֖ם בְּיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ס

passages.text: Judah, your brothers shall praise you. Your hand shall be on the necks of your enemies; your father’s sons shall bow down to you.
passages.sermon:
Judah is a son of Jacob.
Judah’s brothers will praise him.
Judah will have power over his enemies.
Judah’s hand will be on the necks of his enemies.
The sons of Judah’s father will bow down to Judah.
passages.original: יְהוּדָ֗ה אַתָּה֙ יוֹד֣וּךָ אַחֶ֔יךָ יָדְךָ֖ בְּעֹ֣רֶף אֹיְבֶ֑יךָ יִשְׁתַּחֲוּ֥וּ לְךָ֖ בְּנֵ֥י אָבִֽיךָ׃

passages.text: Judah is a young lion— my son, you return from the prey. Like a lion he crouches and lies down; like a lioness, who dares to rouse him?
passages.sermon:
Judah is like a young lion.
Judah is strong and bold.
My son, you have returned from the prey.
Judah crouches like a lion.
Judah lies down like a lioness.
No one dares to wake him.
passages.original: גּ֤וּר אַרְיֵה֙ יְהוּדָ֔ה מִטֶּ֖רֶף בְּנִ֣י עָלִ֑יתָ כָּרַ֨ע רָבַ֧ץ כְּאַרְיֵ֛ה וּכְלָבִ֖יא מִ֥י יְקִימֶֽנּוּ׃

passages.text: The scepter will not depart from Judah, nor the staff from between his feet, until Shiloh comes and the allegiance of the nations is his.
passages.sermon:
Judah is a son of Jacob.
Judah will hold the scepter.
Judah will keep the ruler’s staff between his feet.
Judah’s rule will not end.
This will continue until Shiloh comes.
Shiloh will receive the obedience of the nations.
passages.original: לֹֽא־ יָס֥וּר שֵׁ֙בֶט֙ מִֽיהוּדָ֔ה וּמְחֹקֵ֖ק מִבֵּ֣ין רַגְלָ֑יו עַ֚ד כִּֽי־ יָבֹ֣א שִׁילֹה וְל֖וֹ יִקְּהַ֥ת עַמִּֽים׃

passages.text: He ties his donkey to the vine, his colt to the choicest branch. He washes his garments in wine, his robes in the blood of grapes.
passages.sermon:
Judah is the subject of this blessing.
Judah ties his donkey to a vine.
He ties his colt to the best branch.
He washes his clothes in wine.
He washes his robes in the blood of grapes.
passages.original: אֹסְרִ֤י לַגֶּ֙פֶן֙ עִירֹה וְלַשֹּׂרֵקָ֖ה בְּנִ֣י אֲתֹנ֑וֹ כִּבֵּ֤ס בַּיַּ֙יִן֙ לְבֻשׁ֔וֹ וּבְדַם־ עֲנָבִ֖ים סוּתֹה׃

passages.text: His eyes are darker than wine, and his teeth are whiter than milk.
passages.sermon: This passage describes the ruler from the tribe of Judah.\r\nHis eyes are darker than wine.\r\nHis teeth are whiter than milk.
passages.original: חַכְלִילִ֥י עֵינַ֖יִם מִיָּ֑יִן וּלְבֶן־ שִׁנַּ֖יִם מֵחָלָֽב׃פ

passages.text: Zebulun shall dwell by the seashore and become a harbor for ships; his border shall extend to Sidon.
passages.sermon:
Zebulun is a tribe of Israel.
Zebulun will live by the seashore.
Zebulun will have a place for ships to come.
Zebulun’s border will reach to Sidon.
passages.original: זְבוּלֻ֕ן לְח֥וֹף יַמִּ֖ים יִשְׁכֹּ֑ן וְהוּא֙ לְח֣וֹף אֳנִיּ֔וֹת וְיַרְכָת֖וֹ עַל־ צִידֹֽן׃ס

passages.text: Issachar is a strong donkey, lying down between the sheepfolds.
passages.sermon:
Issachar is a man from the tribes of Israel.
Issachar is strong like a donkey.
Issachar lies down between the sheepfolds.
He rests in a place of work and peace.
passages.original: יִשָּׂשכָ֖ר חֲמֹ֣ר גָּ֑רֶם רֹבֵ֖ץ בֵּ֥ין הַֽמִּשְׁפְּתָֽיִם׃

passages.text: He saw that his resting place was good and that his land was pleasant, so he bent his shoulder to the burden and submitted to labor as a servant.
passages.sermon:
Issachar is a strong donkey.
He lies down between the sheepfolds.
He saw that his resting place was good.
He saw that his land was pleasant.
He bent his shoulder to bear a burden.
He became a servant under forced labor.
passages.original: וַיַּ֤רְא מְנֻחָה֙ כִּ֣י ט֔וֹב וְאֶת־ הָאָ֖רֶץ כִּ֣י נָעֵ֑מָה וַיֵּ֤ט שִׁכְמוֹ֙ לִסְבֹּ֔ל וַיְהִ֖י לְמַס־ עֹבֵֽד׃ס

passages.text: Dan shall provide justice for his people as one of the tribes of Israel.
passages.sermon: Dan is one of the tribes of Israel.\r\nDan will provide justice for his people.\r\nDan will judge his people like the other tribes of Israel.
passages.original: דָּ֖ן יָדִ֣ין עַמּ֑וֹ כְּאַחַ֖ד שִׁבְטֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: He will be a snake by the road, a viper in the path that bites the horse’s heels so that its rider tumbles backward.
passages.sermon:
Dan is like a snake by the road.
Dan is like a viper in the path.
Dan bites the heels of a horse.
The rider falls backward.
passages.original: יְהִי־ דָן֙ נָחָ֣שׁ עֲלֵי־ דֶ֔רֶךְ שְׁפִיפֹ֖ן עֲלֵי־ אֹ֑רַח הַנֹּשֵׁךְ֙ עִקְּבֵי־ ס֔וּס וַיִּפֹּ֥ל רֹכְב֖וֹ אָחֽוֹר׃

passages.text: I await Your salvation, O LORD.
passages.sermon:
The speaker addresses the LORD.
The speaker waits for salvation.
The speaker hopes for the LORD’s deliverance.
passages.original: לִֽישׁוּעָתְךָ֖ קִוִּ֥יתִי יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: Gad will be attacked by raiders, but he will attack their heels.
passages.sermon:
Gad is a person.
Gad will face attacks from raiders.
Raiders will come against Gad.
Gad will strike back.
Gad will attack the raiders at their heels.
passages.original: גָּ֖ד גְּד֣וּד יְגוּדֶ֑נּוּ וְה֖וּא יָגֻ֥ד עָקֵֽב׃ס

passages.text: Asher’s food will be rich; he shall provide royal delicacies.
passages.sermon:
Asher is a son of Jacob.
Asher will have rich food.
Asher will give food fit for a king.
Asher will provide royal delicacies.
passages.original: מֵאָשֵׁ֖ר שְׁמֵנָ֣ה לַחְמ֑וֹ וְה֥וּא יִתֵּ֖ן מַֽעֲדַנֵּי־ מֶֽלֶךְ׃ס

passages.text: Naphtali is a doe set free that bears beautiful fawns.
passages.sermon:
Naphtali is a person.
Naphtali is like a doe.
The doe is free.
Naphtali gives beautiful words.
Naphtali speaks with grace.
passages.original: נַפְתָּלִ֖י אַיָּלָ֣ה שְׁלֻחָ֑ה הַנֹּתֵ֖ן אִמְרֵי־ שָֽׁפֶר׃ס

passages.text: Joseph is a fruitful vine— a fruitful vine by a spring, whose branches scale the wall.
passages.sermon: Joseph is like a fruitful vine.\r\nHe grows by a spring.\r\nHis branches climb over the wall.
passages.original: בֵּ֤ן פֹּרָת֙ יוֹסֵ֔ף בֵּ֥ן פֹּרָ֖ת עֲלֵי־ עָ֑יִן בָּנ֕וֹת צָעֲדָ֖ה עֲלֵי־ שֽׁוּר׃

passages.text: The archers attacked him with bitterness; they aimed at him in hostility.
passages.sermon:
Joseph is the subject.
Many archers attacked Joseph.
They attacked him with bitterness.
They hated him.
They aimed their arrows at him with hostility.
passages.original: וַֽיְמָרֲרֻ֖הוּ וָרֹ֑בּוּ וַֽיִּשְׂטְמֻ֖הוּ בַּעֲלֵ֥י חִצִּֽים׃

passages.text: Yet he steadied his bow, and his strong arms were tempered by the hands of the Mighty One of Jacob, in the name of the Shepherd, the Rock of Israel, by the God of your father who helps you, and by the Almighty who blesses you, with blessings of the heavens above, with blessings of the depths below, with blessings of the breasts and womb.
passages.sermon:
Joseph is the son of Jacob.
Joseph faced many attacks from his enemies.
Joseph remained strong and steady.
He held his bow firmly.
His arms stayed strong.
The Mighty One of Jacob gave him strength.
The Shepherd, the Rock of Israel, helped him.
The God of Joseph’s father helped him.
The Almighty blessed Joseph.
God gave Joseph blessings from the heavens above.
God gave Joseph blessings from the deep waters below.
God gave Joseph blessings of the breasts and the womb.
passages.original: וַתֵּ֤שֶׁב בְּאֵיתָן֙ קַשְׁתּ֔וֹ וַיָּפֹ֖זּוּ זְרֹעֵ֣י יָדָ֑יו מִידֵי֙ אֲבִ֣יר יַעֲקֹ֔ב מִשָּׁ֥ם רֹעֶ֖ה אֶ֥בֶן יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ מֵאֵ֨ל אָבִ֜יךָ וְיַעְזְרֶ֗ךָּ וְאֵ֤ת שַׁדַּי֙ וִיבָ֣רְכֶ֔ךָּ בִּרְכֹ֤ת שָׁמַ֙יִם֙ מֵעָ֔ל בִּרְכֹ֥ת תְּה֖וֹם רֹבֶ֣צֶת תָּ֑חַת בִּרְכֹ֥ת שָׁדַ֖יִם וָרָֽחַם׃

passages.text: The blessings of your father have surpassed the blessings of the ancient mountains and the bounty of the everlasting hills. May they rest on the head of Joseph, on the brow of the prince of his brothers.
passages.sermon:
Jacob is the father of Joseph and his brothers.
Jacob speaks to his sons.
Jacob gives blessings to his sons.
Jacob says his blessings are greater than the blessings of his ancestors.
Jacob says his blessings are greater than the blessings of the ancient mountains.
Jacob says his blessings are greater than the bounty of the everlasting hills.
Jacob asks that these blessings rest on Joseph’s head.
Joseph is the prince among his brothers.
Jacob asks that these blessings rest on the brow of Joseph, the prince of his brothers.
passages.original: בִּרְכֹ֣ת אָבִ֗יךָ גָּֽבְרוּ֙ עַל־ בִּרְכֹ֣ת הוֹרַ֔י עַֽד־ תַּאֲוַ֖ת גִּבְעֹ֣ת עוֹלָ֑ם תִּֽהְיֶ֙ין֙ לְרֹ֣אשׁ יוֹסֵ֔ף וּלְקָדְקֹ֖ד נְזִ֥יר אֶחָֽיו׃פ

passages.text: Benjamin is a ravenous wolf; in the morning he devours the prey, in the evening he divides the plunder.”
passages.sermon:
Benjamin is like a wolf.
He is fierce and hungry.
In the morning, he eats his prey.
In the evening, he shares what he has taken.
passages.original: בִּנְיָמִין֙ זְאֵ֣ב יִטְרָ֔ף בַּבֹּ֖קֶר יֹ֣אכַל עַ֑ד וְלָעֶ֖רֶב יְחַלֵּ֥ק שָׁלָֽל׃

passages.text: These are the tribes of Israel, twelve in all, and this was what their father said to them. He blessed them, and he blessed each one with a suitable blessing.
passages.sermon:
There are twelve tribes of Israel.
These twelve tribes are the sons of Jacob.
Jacob is their father.
Jacob spoke to his sons.
Jacob gave them blessings.
Jacob gave each son a blessing that fit him.
passages.original: כָּל־ אֵ֛לֶּה שִׁבְטֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל שְׁנֵ֣ים עָשָׂ֑ר וְ֠זֹאת אֲשֶׁר־ דִּבֶּ֨ר לָהֶ֤ם אֲבִיהֶם֙ וַיְבָ֣רֶךְ אוֹתָ֔ם אִ֛ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֥ר כְּבִרְכָת֖וֹ בֵּרַ֥ךְ אֹתָֽם׃

passages.text: Then Jacob instructed them, “I am about to be gathered to my people. Bury me with my fathers in the cave in the field of Ephron the Hittite.
passages.sermon:
Jacob was the father of the twelve tribes of Israel.
Jacob spoke to his sons.
Jacob gave them instructions.
Jacob said, “I am about to die.
I will soon join my ancestors.
Bury me with my fathers.
Bury me in the cave.
The cave is in the field of Ephron the Hittite.”
passages.original: וַיְצַ֣ו אוֹתָ֗ם וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲלֵהֶם֙ אֲנִי֙ נֶאֱסָ֣ף אֶל־ עַמִּ֔י קִבְר֥וּ אֹתִ֖י אֶל־ אֲבֹתָ֑י אֶל־ הַ֨מְּעָרָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר בִּשְׂדֵ֖ה עֶפְר֥וֹן הַֽחִתִּֽי׃

passages.text: The cave is in the field of Machpelah near Mamre, in the land of Canaan. This is the field Abraham purchased from Ephron the Hittite as a burial site.
passages.sermon:
The cave is in the field of Machpelah.
This field is near Mamre.
Mamre is in the land of Canaan.
Abraham bought this field from Ephron the Hittite.
Abraham bought it to be a burial site.
passages.original: בַּמְּעָרָ֞ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר בִּשְׂדֵ֧ה הַמַּכְפֵּלָ֛ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר עַל־ פְּנֵי־ מַמְרֵ֖א בְּאֶ֣רֶץ כְּנָ֑עַן אֲשֶׁר֩ קָנָ֨ה אַבְרָהָ֜ם אֶת־ הַשָּׂדֶ֗ה מֵאֵ֛ת עֶפְרֹ֥ן הַחִתִּ֖י לַאֲחֻזַּת־ קָֽבֶר׃

passages.text: There Abraham and his wife Sarah are buried, there Isaac and his wife Rebekah are buried, and there I buried Leah.
passages.sermon:
Abraham is buried there.
Sarah, Abraham’s wife, is buried there.
Isaac is buried there.
Rebekah, Isaac’s wife, is buried there.
I buried Leah there.
passages.original: שָׁ֣מָּה קָֽבְר֞וּ אֶת־ אַבְרָהָ֗ם וְאֵת֙ שָׂרָ֣ה אִשְׁתּ֔וֹ שָׁ֚מָּה קָבְר֣וּ אֶת־ יִצְחָ֔ק וְאֵ֖ת רִבְקָ֣ה אִשְׁתּ֑וֹ וְשָׁ֥מָּה קָבַ֖רְתִּי אֶת־ לֵאָֽה׃

passages.text: The field and the cave that is in it were purchased from the Hittites.”
passages.sermon: Abraham purchased the field from the Hittites.\r\nThe cave is inside this field.\r\nAbraham bought both the field and the cave from the Hittites.
passages.original: מִקְנֵ֧ה הַשָּׂדֶ֛ה וְהַמְּעָרָ֥ה אֲשֶׁר־ בּ֖וֹ מֵאֵ֥ת בְּנֵי־ חֵֽת׃

passages.text: When Jacob had finished instructing his sons, he pulled his feet into the bed and breathed his last, and he was gathered to his people.
passages.sermon:
Jacob was the father of the twelve tribes of Israel.
Jacob finished giving instructions to his sons.
Jacob pulled his feet into the bed.
Jacob breathed his last.
Jacob died.
Jacob was gathered to his people.
passages.original: וַיְכַ֤ל יַעֲקֹב֙ לְצַוֺּ֣ת אֶת־ בָּנָ֔יו וַיֶּאֱסֹ֥ף רַגְלָ֖יו אֶל־ הַמִּטָּ֑ה וַיִּגְוַ֖ע וַיֵּאָ֥סֶף אֶל־ עַמָּֽיו׃
